info.title: Hermed Bots product API (Hermes behind the facade)
info.description:
The surface that a Hermed Bots client (Mac, iOS) uses to read and write on a Hermes instance, through the TLS facade of `scripts/hermes-facade.js`.

**Bot and profile.** One bot is one named Hermes profile. The bot id is the name of the profile, the same string, and it is the `{profile}` segment of every path: `/p/{profile}/...`. The profile `default` is a profile like any other (`/p/default/...`). There is no other way to address a bot. The facade also forwards the unprefixed routes as an alias of `default`: they are not part of this contract.

**Authentication.** Every route except `facade.enrol` needs `Authorization: Bearer <device token>`. A device gets its token once, from `facade.enrol`, with a one-time code that an admin creates. A client never holds the Hermes API key: the facade holds it, replaces the authorization on each request, and never sends it to a device. A Hermes 401 or redirect reaches the device as a 502.

**Reads and writes.** A read is a `GET`. A write is a `POST` and needs an `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 128 visible ASCII characters). The key is kept 24 hours, per device, method and path. The same key and the same body return the kept answer with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. The same key with another body returns 409, when the facade kept the fingerprint of the first body. If the facade cannot know whether Hermes ran the write, it returns 502 `write_outcome_unknown` and never sends that key to Hermes again: the client reads the state (`run.get`, `session.messages`), then sends a new write with a new key if the first one did not happen. The operation id of a write is the id in its answer (`run_id`, `session.id`): a replay returns the same one. The facade has no lookup from a key to its answer.

**Errors.** The facade writes its own errors as `{"error": "<code>"}` (see `FacadeError`). Every other answer of Hermes passes through with its status and its body, except 401 and redirects. A 429 or 408 of Hermes is not kept: the key stays free.

**Limits.** Request body 1 MiB. Per device 20 requests per second (burst 60), writes 5 per second (burst 20). Over the limit: 429 with `Retry-After`.

x-bot-profile-mapping.bot_id: the name of the Hermes profile, the same string
x-bot-profile-mapping.profile: the name of the Hermes profile, the segment after /p/

authority.description: Host and port of the facade, given when the device is enrolled

tags.name: facade
tags.description: Enrolment and device management, handled by the facade itself

get.description: Read the version of Hermes. The status of the profile is `ok` when Hermes answers.

get.summary: Features and routes that Hermes offers
get.description: Lists booleans such as `run_approval_response`, `session_model_lock` and `session_chat`, and the table of routes. It holds no version number.
Answers 200 when Hermes serves the profile. An unknown or parked profile answers 404 with a Hermes body.

post.description: Send a prompt. Hermes answers 202 at once and runs the turn. Follow it with `run.events`. `session_id` continues a session, `model` applies to this run only.

requestBody.description: The prompt, and optionally the session and the model of this run

Idempotency-Replayed.description: `true` when the answer is the kept answer of an earlier send of the same key

get.summary: Read the state of a run
get.description: Use it to read a run after a lost answer. Observed `status` values: `started`, `running`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `interrupted`. The Mac client also reads `failed` and `waiting_for_approval`.

get.summary: Follow a run as an event stream
get.description: Server-sent events as Hermes produces them: `message.delta`, `reasoning.available`, `approval.request`, `approval.responded`, `approval.settled`, `tool.started`, `tool.completed`, `run.completed`, `run.failed`, `run.cancelled`, `run.interrupted`. Hermes 0.22.1 names the id of an approval request `prompt_id` instead of `request_id`. `Last-Event-ID` resumes after the last event received. The facade cuts the stream when the device is revoked.

post.description: Answer the `request_id` of an `approval.request` event with one of its `choices` (`once`, `session`, `always`, `deny`).

Idempotency-Replayed.description: `true` when the answer is the kept answer of an earlier send of the same key

post.description: Hermes answers at once. The run then settles as `cancelled`: read it with `run.get`.

Idempotency-Replayed.description: `true` when the answer is the kept answer of an earlier send of the same key

get.summary: List the past sessions of the bot
get.description: Most recent first. `has_more` tells that another page exists at `offset + limit`.

post.description: An invalid body creates no session.

Idempotency-Replayed.description: `true` when the answer is the kept answer of an earlier send of the same key

get.description: The `model` field shows the model that `session.model` locked, or null when the session follows the model of the profile.

get.summary: Read the messages of a session
get.description: Rows with a role other than `user` and `assistant`, or with no content, are not messages to show.

post.summary: Lock the model of a session
post.description: Applies to the next turns of this session.

Idempotency-Replayed.description: `true` when the answer is the kept answer of an earlier send of the same key

post.summary: Send a prompt and read the whole answer
post.description: Answers once, with no event. It honors the model lock. The streamed variant `chat/stream` is out of this contract: its answer cannot be replayed for an idempotent retry, and the facade answers 404 `route_not_allowed`.

Idempotency-Replayed.description: `true` when the answer is the kept answer of an earlier send of the same key

post.description: Exchange a one-time code for a device token. The code is valid 5 minutes and works once. An unknown, used or expired code gets the same 403. The token is shown once.
Admin role only. The role defaults to `normal`.
Admin role only. The token is refused from the next request, and the event streams of the device are cut within one second.

deviceToken.description: The token returned once by `facade.enrol`, `<device id>.<secret>`

Profile.name: profile
Profile.description: The Hermes profile of the bot: one bot, one profile. The bot id is this name

DeviceId.name: device_id
DeviceId.description: The id of a device, as `facade.devices.list` shows it

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Chosen by the client, new for each write, reused for a retry of the same write

LastEventId.name: Last-Event-ID
LastEventId.description: The id of the last event received

BadRequest.description: A facade 400 (`invalid_query`, `invalid_json`, `invalid_role`, `idempotency_key_required`, `idempotency_key_invalid`), or a 400 of Hermes with its own body

Unauthorized.description: No valid token: missing, malformed, unknown, wrong secret or revoked. Every path answers the same, so a path cannot be probed

Forbidden.description: The role is not admin (`forbidden`), or the enrolment code is unknown, used or expired (`invalid_code`)

NotFound.description: `route_not_allowed` when the facade does not forward the route, `unknown_device`, or a 404 of Hermes: `Unknown or unconfigured profile` (JSON or plain text), `session_not_found`, `run_not_found`

MethodNotAllowed.description: The route exists for another method

Conflict.description: `idempotency_key_conflict`: the key was used with another body. `idempotency_replay_unavailable`: the first answer was over 16 KiB, so the facade did not keep it

RequestTimeout.description: Hermes answered 408: it did not run the write, so the facade keeps nothing and the key stays free. The answer passes through as Hermes sent it, with its `Retry-After`. Send the same key again after the delay

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the next try, when Hermes sends it

PayloadTooLarge.description: The body is over the limit. Hermes is not called

RateLimited.description: The device is over its limit (`rate_limited`), or Hermes asked for a later retry. The key of a write is not kept

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the next try

BadGateway.description: The facade could not get an answer from Hermes: `upstream_unavailable`, `upstream_timeout`, `upstream_rejected` (Hermes refused the key of the facade), `upstream_redirect`, `upstream_key_missing` (no Hermes key for the profile), or `write_outcome_unknown` (a write may have run: do not send its key again). A 502 that Hermes sends on a write passes through with the body of Hermes: tell the two apart by the body

ServiceUnavailable.description: `idempotency_journal_full`: the facade keeps no new key until old ones expire. Hermes is not called. A 503 that Hermes sends on a write passes through with the body of Hermes

HermesServerError.description: A 5xx of Hermes, passed through as Hermes sent it. For a write, the first send gets it and the same key then gets 502 `write_outcome_unknown`

HermesError.description: The body of Hermes, as it sent it. Its shape differs by route: `{"error": "..."}`, `{"error": {"code": "run_not_found", ...}}`, or plain text

Error.description: A facade error, or a body of Hermes. A facade error fits both branches, so the branches are not exclusive

replayed.description: Set by Hermes when it replays its own key

choice.description: One of the `choices` of the event

code.description: The one-time code, with or without dashes

name.description: Name of the device, 64 characters at most

token.description: `<device id>.<secret>`, shown once, stored hashed by the facade
